To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best results are obtained by using the best features, and that the best features are the ones that are specific for the task.

(1) the best results are achieved when the data are lemmatized and when the data are represented as a combination of features; and (2) the best results in terms of sentiment analysis are achieved with a lexicon based method that is combined with a supervised learning approach.

(a) lemmatization improves performance in all tasks, (b) genre-specific features improve performance in all tasks except for subjectivity detection, and (c) dialect-specific features are useful only for subjectivity detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) What features are most useful for sentiment and subjectivity analysis? 2) How can we represent the lexical information? 3) What is the impact of dialectal variation? 4) What is the role of domain and genre specific features? 5) How can we combine the features?
